lead.headline: Telegram's Gram Wallet Rollout Tests Whether Distribution Can Overcome Regulatory Fog
lead.tldr: Telegram is betting that 900 million users and a non-custodial architecture can succeed where its 2019 ICO failed, even as the US advances market-structure legislation and Russia opens regulated retail access—creating divergent regulatory lanes that infrastructure plays must now navigate simultaneously.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Telegram is attempting the largest non-custodial wallet deployment in history while Washington and Moscow both rewrite the rules of access, so today's brief tracks how distribution scale and regulatory fragmentation are colliding in real time.

top_signals.title: Telegram plans 'largest rollout of a non-custodial crypto wallet in human history'
top_signals.summary: Telegram is planning a massive rollout of a non-custodial crypto wallet to its vast user base. The move is seen as a significant effort to onboard a mainstream audience into the cryptocurrency ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The 'largest rollout' framing matters because Telegram is explicitly testing whether user base scale can substitute for the compliance-heavy onboarding that has bottlenecked every prior mass-market wallet attempt, and the non-custodial architecture is a direct hedge against the regulatory exposure that killed its 2019 Gram token sale.

top_signals.title: Pavel Durov says Telegram to roll out native Gram crypto wallet22m
top_signals.summary: Telegram CEO Pavel Durov announced the rollout of a native crypto wallet for the Gram token. This integration aims to bring cryptocurrency functionality directly into the messaging platform's ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Durov's native Gram wallet announcement confirms the wallet will be token-specific rather than multi-chain, which means Telegram is underwriting the thesis that a closed-loop messaging economy can generate sufficient transaction velocity to justify the infrastructure investment without needing broad DeFi interoperability.

top_signals.title: Solana, Hyperliquid ETFs dominate altcoin fund flows despite flying under the radar
top_signals.summary: Solana and Hyperliquid ETFs are seeing significant capital inflows, signaling strong institutional interest in altcoin assets. Solana ETFs have reached $904 million in AUM, while Hyperliquid funds have seen $350 million in net inflows.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Solana and Hyperliquid ETFs commanding $1.25 billion in combined flows while 'flying under the radar' suggests institutional allocation to altcoin beta is happening faster than sell-side coverage can model, which typically precedes either a repricing event or a sharp correction when the lagged narrative catches up.

top_signals.title: Russia passes landmark crypto bill allowing regulated retail trading
top_signals.summary: Russia's State Duma has passed a landmark bill that establishes a legal framework for regulated retail cryptocurrency trading. The law introduces specific purchase limits for non-qualified investors to manage risk.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Russia's retail trading limits for non-qualified investors create a template for how major economies can permit crypto access without fully liberalizing it, and any infrastructure or exchange play with Russian exposure now has a testable regulatory framework to underwrite against rather than pure speculation.

top_signals.title: White House Agrees to Ethics Provisions in Market Structure Bill
top_signals.summary: The White House has reached an agreement on ethics provisions within a proposed crypto market structure bill. This compromise removes a significant hurdle for Democratic support of the legislation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The White House ethics compromise on market structure legislation removes the last identifiable Democratic procedural objection, which means the bill's passage probability has shifted materially and any US-facing exchange or custody business should now be modeling compliance costs against a statutory rather than enforcement-only regime.

deals.summary: Digital Asset, the developer of the Canton Network, has secured an additional $10 million in funding. The investment comes from Shinhan Financial Group and SC Ventures at a maintained equity valuation of $2 billion.

on_the_radar.title: CoinShares launches UCITS platform targeting Europe's institutional investors
on_the_radar.summary: CoinShares is launching a new platform targeting Europe's $30 trillion UCITS ecosystem to attract institutional investors. The expansion includes the introduction of a Bitcoin Mining ETF.

on_the_radar.title: Grayscale files S-1 for first US Worldcoin ETF23m, Grayscale files S-1 for first US Worldcoin ETFThe filing expands Grayscale’s growing lineup of crypto-related exchange-traded products outside of Bitcoin and Ether.
on_the_radar.summary: Grayscale has filed an S-1 registration statement to launch the first US-based Worldcoin ETF. This move expands Grayscale's suite of digital asset products beyond its existing Bitcoin and Ether offerings.

on_the_radar.title: Base Creator Says 1:1-Backed Tokenized Equities Launch Is ‘Imminent’
on_the_radar.summary: Base creator Jesse Pollak announced that the launch of 1:1-backed tokenized equities on the Ethereum layer-2 network is imminent. This move signals a strategic pivot for Base toward trading and the integration of real-world tokenized assets.

on_the_radar.title: Russia Completes Final Readings on Crypto Regulation Bill
on_the_radar.summary: Russia's State Duma has completed the final readings of a comprehensive cryptocurrency bill. The legislation aims to establish a regulatory framework for crypto assets, market participants, and trading operations within the country.

on_the_radar.title: CLARITY Act Could Help CFTC Deal with Prediction Markets: Lawyer
on_the_radar.summary: A US House subcommittee held a hearing to discuss the CFTC's oversight of prediction markets and the potential impact of the CLARITY Act. The legislation aims to provide clearer regulatory frameworks for these markets.

on_the_radar.title: U.N. reports Southeast Asia’s criminal networks are using tech to build a global illicit economy
on_the_radar.summary: A U.N. report highlights how criminal networks in Southeast Asia are leveraging technology to scale a global illicit economy. These operations resulted in an estimated $114.1 billion in losses last year through expanded scamming activities.

on_the_radar.title: Trump-backed crypto ethics rule puts DOJ in charge of enforcement, prohibits federal officials from issuing cryptocurrencies
on_the_radar.summary: President Donald Trump has signed new ethics rules that prohibit federal officials from issuing cryptocurrencies. The rules also designate the Department of Justice (DOJ) as the primary body responsible for enforcement.

on_the_radar.title: The Digital Chamber sues Illinois over incoming crypto transaction tax
on_the_radar.summary: The Digital Chamber is filing a lawsuit against the state of Illinois to challenge a new law. The legal action targets a proposed 0.2% tax on digital asset transactions.

linkedin_post:
Telegram tried to sell Gram tokens in 2019. The SEC stopped it. Now Durov is back with a non-custodial wallet for those same tokens, baked into 900 million active messaging accounts. The architecture changed; the regulatory exposure did not, it shifted. Non-custodial means no licensed custody, no money-transmitter nexus, no obvious SEC hook. That is not a loophole, it is a design choice, and it will be tested immediately.

What is different this time is the competitive set. In 2019 Telegram was early. In 2025 every major messaging app has some payment rail, and the US is three procedural votes from a statutory market-structure regime that would legitimize onshore exchange competition. Russia just opened regulated retail access with purchase caps. The lanes are diverging: permissioned in Moscow, rule-bound in Washington, architecture-first in Dubai where Telegram sits.

We underwrite infrastructure on regulatory clarity and user acquisition cost. Telegram's user acquisition cost for this wallet is effectively zero. Its regulatory clarity is deliberately thin. That asymmetry is the bet.

The test: if Gram wallet transaction volume fails to correlate with Telegram's existing peer-to-peer payment behavior, the token becomes a speculative appendage rather than a utility layer, and the non-custodial shield will not matter. We are watching Q3 on-chain data. If the volume is there, the model spreads. If not, this joins the file of distribution-without-demand cases that crypto keeps producing.
